## Purpose and entry points
Kamailio is a C-based, scalable SIP signaling server for VoIP, messaging, and presence. The executable starts in `src/main.c`; its behavior is primarily defined by a runtime routing configuration such as `etc/kamailio.cfg`. Build entry points are `CMakeLists.txt` and `src/CMakeLists.txt`; installed operations are supported by `utils/kamctl/kamctl` and `utils/kamcmd/kamcmd.c`.

## Startup, configuration, and module loading
Startup initializes daemon/process infrastructure, parses the native configuration language, loads configured modules, and registers their exported commands, parameters, RPCs, and routing hooks. The configuration grammar and parser are `src/core/cfg.lex`, `src/core/cfg.y`, and `src/core/cfg_parser.c`; module ABI/registration is centered on `src/core/sr_module.c`. This is the principal extension boundary: core supplies stable APIs while selected shared modules implement features.

## SIP ingress-to-egress pipeline
Network listeners accept SIP over UDP and TCP (with optional SCTP/TLS/WebSocket support), parse a message, execute configured route blocks, then send or relay resulting requests/replies. Key stages are `src/core/receive.c`, `src/core/parser/msg_parser.c`, `src/core/route.c`, and `src/core/forward.c`. Message modifications are represented as deferred “lumps” (`src/core/data_lump.c`), separating script/module transformations from final wire serialization.

## Stateful signaling and routing policy
The core supports stateless forwarding, while optional modules add transaction, dialog, registrar, and destination-selection state. The transaction manager owns branch/reply/timer behavior in `src/modules/tm/tm.c` and `src/modules/tm/t_reply.c`; dialog tracking is in `src/modules/dialog/dialog.c`. Registration flows typically cross `src/modules/registrar/registrar.c` into `src/modules/usrloc/usrloc.c`. Routing policy modules such as dispatcher and dialplan consume configured or database-backed destinations: `src/modules/dispatcher/dispatcher.c` and `src/modules/drouting/drouting.c`.

## Persistence and distributed integrations
Database access is abstracted behind the `srdb1` library (`src/lib/srdb1/db.c`, `src/lib/srdb1/db.h`), with loadable adapters for MySQL, PostgreSQL, Redis, MongoDB, SQLite, text files, Oracle, and ODBC; representative drivers are `src/modules/db_mysql/db_mysql.c` and `src/modules/db_redis/db_redis_mod.c`. Canonical schemas are XML definitions under `src/lib/srdb1/schema/`, rendered into backend-specific creation scripts under `utils/kamctl/mysql/` and peers. Optional modules connect to Diameter/IMS, RADIUS, LDAP, HTTP, Kafka, RabbitMQ, NATS, MQTT, and RTP relays; these are deployment-selected dependencies, not mandatory runtime services.

## Control plane, observability, and scripting
The core RPC interface (`src/core/rpc.h`) is exposed through selectable transports, including control sockets (`src/modules/ctl/ctl.c`), JSON-RPC (`src/modules/jsonrpcs/jsonrpcs_mod.c`), and HTTP RPC (`src/modules/xhttp_rpc/xhttp_rpc.c`). Metrics and tracing are opt-in modules, including Prometheus HTTP export (`src/modules/xhttp_prom/xhttp_prom.c`) and SIP trace/capture (`src/modules/siptrace/siptrace.c`). KEMI provides an alternate routing-programming boundary; `src/core/kemi.c`/`src/core/kemiexec.c` are backed by language modules such as Lua, JavaScript, Python, and Ruby.

## Runtime and delivery model
The server is native C with a multi-process/shared-memory design: process management is in `src/core/pt.c`, shared memory in `src/core/mem/shm.c`, and timers/event waiting in `src/core/timer.c` and `src/core/io_wait.c`. TLS is modular, with OpenSSL and wolfSSL implementations under `src/modules/tls/` and `src/modules/tls_wolfssl/`. Packaging targets Linux distributions and systemd, e.g. `pkg/kamailio/deb/debian/kamailio.service`; CMake also detects optional external libraries through `cmake/modules/`.
